details.description: Gemma 3 12B is an instruction-tuned, open-weight multimodal model in Google DeepMind's Gemma 3 family, accepting text and image input and producing text output over a 128K-token context window. It was trained on 12 trillion tokens with an August 2024 knowledge cutoff and supports data in over 140 languages, per Google's model card. Google's current developer docs now group Gemma 3 under "previous Gemma models," with Gemma 4 listed as the current generation, though Gemma 3's weights remain downloadable.
advantages: Scores 85.4 on HumanEval (0-shot) and 94.4 on GSM8K (0-shot), per Google's Gemma 3 model card.
Scores 40.9 on GPQA Diamond and 60.6 on MMLU (Pro), per Google's Gemma 3 model card.
Trained on data spanning over 140 languages, per Google's Gemma 3 model card.
Handles text and image input, encoding each image at 896x896 resolution as 256 tokens, per Google's model card.
disadvantages: Superseded by Gemma 4, which Google's developer docs list as the current Gemma generation, with Gemma 3 grouped under "previous Gemma models."
No function calling or tool-use capability is documented for this model on Google's model card; Google offers a separate FunctionGemma variant for that.
Knowledge cutoff of August 2024, per Google's model card.
Google's model card notes the model can struggle with nuance, sarcasm, or figurative language, and may generate incorrect or outdated factual statements.
use_cases: Question answering and image content analysis
Creative text generation such as poems, scripts, and marketing copy

notes: Catalog's max_output_tokens (8000) is close to, but not identical to, Google's stated 8,192-token max output for Gemma 3 12B IT; kept the catalog's value per instructions. Google's ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/core page now lists Gemma 4 as the current generation and groups Gemma 3 under 'Previous Gemma models,' though no formal deprecation date is stated for Gemma 3 itself and its weights remain available. The Hugging Face card also carries a separate, much lower benchmark table for the base ('PT') checkpoint (e.g. HumanEval 45.7 vs 85.4); evaluations above use only the instruction-tuned ('IT') numbers from Google's official model card, which match the IT-labeled rows on the Hugging Face card.
